question.text: <math> <mrow> <mtext>0</mtext><mtext>.15</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>g</mtext></mrow> </math> of a substance dissolved in <math> <mrow> <mtext>15</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>g</mtext></mrow> </math> of solvent boiled at a temperature higher by <math><mn>0.21</mn><msup><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> than that of the pure solvent. The molecular weight of the substance is [Given: Molal elevation constant for the solvent is <math> <mrow> <mtext>2</mtext><mtext>.16</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>Kkg</mtext><mtext> </mtext><msup> <mrow> <mtext>mol</mtext></mrow> <mrow> <mo>−</mo><mtext>1</mtext></mrow> </msup> </mrow> </math>]

solution.text:
Here it is given that w = 0.15 g,   ΔT b  = 0 .216 o C
W = 15 g,  K b  = 2.16 Kkg  mol −1
Substituting values in the expression, m=1000×Kb×wΔTb×W
m =  1000×216×0.15 0.216×15 =100 g/mol
